report.summary: Three Earth twins are offered. Albania matches best on terrain shape, but its similarity is modest. Each site has a clear terrain weakness that the campaign should account for.

claims.text: Albania (earth-945271) is the closest terrain match to the Shackleton rim, with a modest terrain similarity of 0.5656.
Albania is weakest in slope steepness, with mean slope 20.9° on the Moon against 12.9° at the Albania site.
Italy (earth-956430) has a modest terrain similarity of 0.5218, and its main weakness is roughness, with 12 km roughness of 635 m RMS against 373 m.
Switzerland (earth-229110) has a modest terrain similarity of 0.5080, closest on slope and relief, but it differs in curvature (41% vs 47% of area convex) and 12 km roughness (635 m vs 404 m RMS).

report.summary: Target sun stays near the horizon, never above 5 degrees in the analytic model. Earth twins score high on light_sim but have much higher median sun elevation, so they cannot reproduce low-sun conditions. Mars light is unassessed.

claims.text: The target's sun-elevation histogram puts half the time below the horizon and the other half between 0 and 5 degrees, with nothing above 5 degrees.

Albania's light_sim of 0.8618551587301574 is high, but its median sun elevation is far above the target's and a substantial share of time sits between 15 and 60 degrees, so it does not reproduce the target's low sun.

Italy and Switzerland show the same pattern, with light_sim values of 0.8645833333333324 and 0.8767857142857104 and median sun elevations well above the target's, so their similarity scores overstate light match, and their proposed windows are 12-04 to 12-31 and 12-10 to 01-06.
The Mars twin has light_sim null, so its sun regime cannot be assessed here, though its terrain_sim of 0.7293097262582366 is the highest of the candidates.

The site finder candidate sp-0648-0631 gets 14.9 percent sun but fails the 10-degree slope limit at 32.06 degrees mean slope, so it is not proposed; the light model is analytic with no local horizon or terrain shadowing, which matters on this polar rim.

report.summary: Test plan for the Shackleton rim: low-sun drill and slope traverse at the Switzerland twin, terrain-only drill at the Mars twin, shadowed-area work kept limited because the candidate fails the slope limit. Earth twins match terrain and light only partly.

claims.text: Run the low-sun navigation drill at the Switzerland twin during its 12-10 to 01-06 window, since it has the highest light similarity of the three Earth twins.

Run the slope traverse at the Switzerland twin, because the pair comparison puts its mean slope at 15.0° against 20.9° on the lunar ground, while candidate sp-0648-0631 fails the slope limit and should stay out of traverse work.
Run a terrain-only ground handling drill at the Mars twin, which has the top terrain score in the pack but no light match, so it tests the ground without lighting conditions.
Run shadowed-area operations on the lunar candidate only in a limited setting, since its permanently shadowed region is close but no Earth twin in the pack reproduces that shadow.

sites.label: Albania twin
sites.context: Best Earth match on terrain shape (rank 1, score 0.6841). Closest in topographic position and slope-direction variety, but gentler slopes (12.9° vs 20.9°) and much less local relief (1524 m vs 2470 m).
sites.role_in_campaign: Primary terrain-shape site for navigation and route planning over rises and hollows, plus a sun-elevation calibration site.

sites.label: Switzerland twin
sites.context: Highest light_sim of the three Earth twins and closest on slope (15.0° vs 20.9°) and relief (2115 m vs 2470 m). Weaker on curvature and 12 km roughness. No light histogram for this site is in the pack.
sites.role_in_campaign: Site for the low-sun drill and slope traverse, with its light match treated as unverified.

sites.label: Mars twin
sites.context: Highest terrain_sim in the pack, but light_sim is null, so its sun regime cannot be assessed. It is not reachable for field work in the same way as the Earth twins.
sites.role_in_campaign: Terrain-only ground handling analogue for modelling and simulation, with no lighting claims.

tests.name: Low-sun navigation drill
tests.why: The target's sun is below the horizon half the time and between 0 and 5 degrees for the rest. Switzerland has the best light_sim, so it gives the closest available practice in long-shadow and glare navigation, even though real sun elevation there is higher.

tests.name: Slope traverse
tests.why: Switzerland is closest on mean slope and relief. The site finder candidate fails the slope limit, so traverse practice happens on the Earth twin rather than the lunar candidate.

tests.name: Topographic-position navigation and route planning
tests.why: Albania is the best terrain-shape match, with the closest topographic position and slope-direction variety. It tests route choices over rises and hollows, with slope steepness and relief as known gaps.

tests.name: Sun-elevation calibration
tests.why: Earth light_sim scores overstate the match, because the Albania median sun elevation (28.09°) is far above the target's (1.07°). Measuring actual sun angles and shadows there quantifies how far the low-sun drill falls short.

tests.name: Terrain-only ground handling
tests.why: The Mars twin has the strongest terrain score in the pack but no light data, so it tests ground handling without any lighting claim.

disagreements.about: Which Earth twin leads the campaign: Albania (best terrain_sim) or Switzerland (best light_sim, closest slope and relief).
disagreements.resolution: Split. Albania carries terrain-shape navigation and sun calibration. Switzerland carries the low-sun drill and slope traverse. Neither is treated as a full match for the Shackleton rim.

disagreements.about: Whether high Earth light_sim justifies the low-sun drill. Light says the scores overstate the match; the Test Lead uses Switzerland's score to place the drill.
disagreements.resolution: Keep the drill at Switzerland, but pair it with sun-elevation calibration at Albania, and record that the pack has no light histogram for Switzerland, so its sun elevation is unverified.

disagreements.about: Whether the Mars twin belongs in the plan: highest terrain_sim, but no light data and ranked last by logistics.
disagreements.resolution: Keep it for one terrain-only test with no lighting claims. Italy is dropped because its roughness gap (12 km roughness 635 m vs 373 m RMS) and similar light profile to Albania give it no distinct role.

not_reproducible_on_earth: Lunar gravity, which is much weaker than Earth's, so walking and load handling cannot be matched.
Hard vacuum, so there is no air for sound, cooling, or dust-free handling.
Permanently shadowed cold ground near the pole, which no Earth twin in the pack reproduces.
Regolith dust that clings and abrades, unlike Earth soils.
Radiation at the surface with no atmosphere or magnetic shield.
limitations: Sunlight uses an analytic model: circular orbit, no eccentricity, no local horizon or terrain shadowing.
Similarity is terrain shape only (slope, roughness, relief, curvature); not geology, chemistry or regolith.
Terrain is compared at one common ground scale; features smaller than the grid spacing are not seen.
Environment data (country, climate, airport) is a coarse proxy for logistics; no routing or permits checked.
No ctx items in the pack, so country, climate, elevation and airport access are unknown for every site.
The light model is analytic with no local horizon or terrain shadowing, which matters on a polar rim.
No light histogram is in the pack for the Switzerland twin, so its sun elevation is unverified.
The Mars twin has no light_sim.
Site finder candidate sp-0648-0631 fails the slope limit and is not used as a site.
